text:
tom: noticed a burst of KMS Decrypts from private cluster 'onprem-west' around 03:05 UTC, alerted by our KMS audit shipper. any ideas? :wave:
anika: can you paste the audit sample?
tom: `2026-03-20T03:05:12Z KMSDecrypt key=projects/private-kms/keys/pkey-3 caller=serviceAccount:onprem:redwood-agent`
ryan: that SA should only have wrapping permissions. weird if it's calling Decrypt. could be a mis-scoped CRB or an IAM condition missing.
selene: checking cluster: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding | grep redwood-agent` -> nothing obvious, but there is `ci-adhoc-crb` created 03:02 by pipeline user `infra-gitlab`
ops-oncall: recommend temporary isolation: 1) revoke SA tokens for redwood-agent, 2) apply Namespace NetworkPolicy default-deny egress, 3) delete suspicious CRB, 4) pull full KMS and apiserver audit, 5) rotate key if unknown decrypts continued.
anika: running commands now - delete secret for SA and remove CRB.
ryan: dropping a minimal netpol snippet here; note we prefer DNS names resolved to internal proxy IP to avoid dns-evasion:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: onprem-temporary-egress-deny
  namespace: onprem
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
selene: applied netpol -> egress blocked across namespace. observed KMS decrypt spikes stopped within 30s. ops-oncall: created ticket SEC-2026-4991 and set state -> mitigated.
tom: root cause tentative: CI job `infra-gitlab` created CRB due to a permissive pipeline template. privilege escalation vector: CI token allowed CRB create.
ryan: mitigation ideas: enforce OPA/Conftest gate on pipelines to deny CRB/ClusterRole grants, require human approval for any CRB creation, and add an IAM Condition on KMS keys binding allowed 'serviceAccount' with expected namespace label.
anika: also propose enhanced audit: stream KMS Admin logs to SIEM with alert rule: kms.decrypt_count > 50/min for private clusters.
selene: follow-ups: 1) inventory CRBs created by CI in last 14 days, 2) add pipeline linting rule to block `kubectl create clusterrolebinding`, 3) template safe-role for CI that uses Role/RoleBinding only, 4) update runbook with netpol fallback and SA token revocation steps.
ops-oncall: note added to ticket: "Apply netpol fallback, revoke SA secrets, delete CRB, capture KMS + kube-audit timeline, rotate keys if anomaly persists."
tom: one policy proposal: default egress-deny for all private clusters with an allowlist svc/proxy and documented exception process. higher isolation but safer.
ryan: agree but need staged rollout and compatibility tests. create canary in staging-private first.
sec-bot: creating follow-up epic EPIC-PRIVSEC-88 assigned to anika/ryan/selene.
tom: thanks everyone. closing thread after attaching logs to SEC-2026-4991. :thumbsup:
